skeleton.label: Spine-anchored
skeleton.note: Rigid fit of the vertebrae T10-L4 (method A1) mapping each date into the Sep 2026 frame. The spine lines up (residual = mean spine landmark error); the liver does NOT: the patient breathed differently on each date (right liver dome 69 / 89 / 78 mm above T12 on May / June / Sep), so the liver is off by ~11 mm (May) and ~12 mm (June) in this mode.

liver.label: Liver-anchored
liver.note: Rigid fit anchored on the liver (method B1: liver dome + lesion centroids) mapping each date into the Sep 2026 frame. The liver lines up better (residual = mean liver landmark error, 4 landmarks, three of them lesion centroids confounded by growth); the spine is then off by ~16 mm (May) and ~9 mm (June). Use for lesion position comparison, never for volumes.

registration.source: registration.json (recommended: anatomical=A1, liver=B1); matrices map each date's RAS mm into the sep2026 RAS mm frame, row-major 4x4
caveats: Respiratory state differs between the dates (relative to T12: right liver dome +69 mm May, +89 mm June, +78 mm Sep; spleen tip and left kidney follow the same pattern). No single rigid/affine transform aligns both skeleton and liver: skeleton-anchored transforms leave ~10-12 mm liver error, liver-anchored ones leave ~8-11 mm spine error.

Liver-anchored accuracy evidence is thin: 4 liver landmarks per pair (dome z-only, S8 dome-lesion centroid, left-lesion centroid, dominant-mass centroid). Three are lesion centroids and therefore confounded by growth; on Sep (non-contrast, 3.27 mm slices) the S8 lesion boundary is faint and its centroid is uncertain by ~5 mm.
C, C_affine_only and Cr were fitted on the dominant-mass and left-lesion surfaces, so their rmass_center/llesion_center TRE is not independent (listed as circular).

Affine variants change size: B2 (may) singular values 1.067/1.008/0.954 (det 1.026), C/C_affine_only (jun) det 0.926. Do not use affine-mapped meshes for volume/growth numbers; measure volumes natively per date.

The skeleton landmarks (endplates, spinous tip) lie on the vertebrae whose TS-seed surfaces A1-A3 were fitted to; they are placed from CT intensity/visual checks, not from the seeds, but they are not fully independent of A.
Landmark localisation uncertainty: ~1-2 mm (endplates, contrast studies), ~2-3 mm in z on Sep (3.27 mm step, 3.75 mm thick slices), ~3-5 mm for organ poles/tips and lesion centroids.

jun2026 PET (suv_on_ct.nii.gz) is ~2 cm off its own venous CT in the liver (see studies/jun2026/meta.json); these matrices map the CT frame. Use suv_on_ct_liverreg for June liver SUV before applying them.

notes: Consensus masks (consensus/<date>/masks, one review round each; May two). Unresolved challenge points are shown as confidence labels on the layers and lesions (per_date.confidence), not fixed: segments are inferred (automatic, not vessel-guided) on June and Sep and partly inferred on May; hepatic veins are low confidence on June and Sep and incomplete on May.
June left hepatic vein vs the left lesion: they touch; encirclement is not established either way (June challenge C01).

June active: the 1.0 mL P3 patch on the right-mass medial-superior wall (8 mm snap rule, mostly below SUV 2.12; challenge C02) was moved out of the active mask into consensus/jun2026/uncertain/ and is shown only as the Uncertainty layer "FDG activity, inferred only".
FDG-active tissue outside the CT lesion masks is shown as its own layer "PET-defined only" (June 5.5 mL, Sep 18.5 mL): the PET defines its extent, the CT shows no boundary.

Lesion IDs follow the consensus lesion_ids numbering across dates (R1, L1, S8 dome, S7sat, S1 caudate, K, N; Sep P7 is new and provisional); lesions[].match gives the confidence of each cross-date correspondence.

Meshes are exact reproductions of the slice masks: marching cubes on the native CT grid (x3 linear interpolation between slices only), light volume-preserving Taubin smoothing (normalize_coordinates), decimation only where a per-structure face cap is set (see BUILD_NOTES.md; verify.decimated); each mesh is voxelised back and compared with its mask (verify.dice, p95 surface distance in mm).
Coordinates are RAS mm of each date's own CT (x patient right, y anterior, z superior); the registration matrices map them into the Sep 2026 frame.

Spine-anchored and liver-anchored views differ because the patient breathed differently on each date (right liver dome 69 / 89 / 78 mm above T12): no single rigid matrix aligns both skeleton and liver.

Growth maps use the liver-anchored (B1) matrices so that liver-internal lesions are compared in a liver frame; the B1 residual (~6-9 mm) is of the same order as real growth, so read growth maps for patterns (one-sided vs uniform), and use the per-date volumes for size change.

Volumes, sizes, HU and SUV are measured natively on each date (no registration). SUV: May/June use suv_on_ct_liverreg (liver-aligned PET), Sep suv_on_ct; PET edges blur ~6 mm; our Sep SUVs may be ~11 % above the report (net vs gross dose).
Sizes are measured the radiologists' way: maximal axial diameter (edge-to-edge on the best axial slice), perpendicular width on that slice, craniocaudal extent.
